compile.globalConstraints:
- No credential anywhere: no `Authorization` header and no bearer in any request the boot makes, no `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` in any file of the tree, in any argv, in any environment the boot exports — the edge injects the bearer, exactly as it does for `claude-max` and `kata`.
- Nothing gates on Jev: no `jev` field is read by the gate verdict, the answer line (`**Merged**`, `**Merge-ready**`, `**Held:**`, `**Parked:**`), the draft flag, the merge PUT, `routeToPlan` or any event kind; a run whose every TypeSafe request fails publishes the same pull request, byte for byte, as one whose requests all succeeded — the `Act on these` section aside.
- The boot's own `kind` rule (`cannot verify` / `could not verify`), the `Residuals: <n> from review` line, the errand lines, the `Amendments:` lines and the record's `### Residuals` checklist render exactly as they do at BASE; the rule is the rollback, with the card section deleted.
- The request seam merged as `4dccc32f` — `residual_read`'s `jev` mode, `residual_jev`, `residuals-jev.jsonl`, `TYPESAFE_URL` — is not changed: no new request is made at render time, and the request count per run stays one per residual.
- No new event kind is appended to `events.jsonl`, no new assignment key is read from the VM comment, no new lobby verb, no new npm dependency, and nothing under `fleet/roles/` changes.
- Findings are about the result — what the card, the sims and the documents now say — never about the order the work was done in, the number of commits, or whether a test was written before its code.

llmDerives: waves[][].tier on the args-file wave entries (slots pre-emitted as null; the engine reads knobs ONLY from these inline entries — never a top-level launch key)

nothing for waves[][].testCmd — the per-task command is compiler-derived from the task's Proof `Test:` paths and pre-filled on the wave entries (run-wide testCmd is driver-derived — knob or detection — and already stamped in the args file and receipt)

nothing for bootstrapCmd — driver-derived from the target's lockfile/manifest (or the --bootstrap-cmd knob) and stamped in the args file and receipt, so validation, the engine and the gate share one value

nothing for addCmd/addDevCmd — the package-add commands are driver-derived from the same lockfile/manifest beside the bootstrap and stamped in the args file and receipt (only when the plan declares packages); there is no knob for them

nothing for regenerateCmd — the lockfile regenerator is derived from the same lockfile/manifest beside the bootstrap (and only when the bootstrap itself was derived) and stamped in the args file and receipt; there is no knob for it
nothing for review depth — it is plan-authored (**Review:** marker), pre-filled on the args wave entries
